text:
# Face Culling and Visibility Optimization

Also called: Interior Polygon Removal, Removing Interior Polygons

## Overview
Face Culling and Visibility Optimization reduces the rendering load of blocky voxel meshes by reconstructing cubes from triangles and removing sides that are adjacent to solid neighbors, thereby avoiding the rendering of hidden geometry [S1, unofficial]. It solves the problem of naively rendering all 6 faces of every voxel, which results in excessive triangle counts (e.g., rendering 12 triangles for a fully internal cube when 0 are visible) [S1, unofficial]. It sets itself apart from sibling methods by performing this check primarily through direct neighbor lookup during mesh creation, rather than using coverage masks, backface culling, or opacity-based thresholds [S1, unofficial].

## Shared principles
The core mechanism involves iterating over every voxel in a chunk or mesh region and evaluating the occupancy of its six immediate neighbors ($\pm X, \pm Y, \pm Z$). A face is generated if and only if the neighbor in that direction is empty (air) or transparent. If the neighbor is solid/opaque, the face is internal and culled [S1, unofficial].

To optimize performance, the meshes of all individual cubes are often combined into a single big mesh called a 'chunk' [S1, unofficial]. This approach allows the culling check to run once during mesh generation, resulting in no framerate loss during rendering [S1, unofficial].

## Subtopics

### [Voxel Block Shape & Culling Configuration](2176-voxel-block-shape-culling-configuration.md)
[Voxel Block Shape & Culling Configuration](2176-voxel-block-shape-culling-configuration.md) is a trait-based system that defines the geometry, transparency culling behavior, and lighting properties for individual block types. It decouples block identity from mesh generation logic, enabling complex shapes and varied [transparency handling](#3611-order-independent-transparency-approaches.md) without large switch statements. It builds on the basic neighbor lookup by providing per-block parameters (e.g., `TransparentMerged` vs `TransparentUnmerged`) that determine how neighbor visibility is interpreted.

### [Face Coverage Mask Culling](3397-face-coverage-mask-culling.md)
[Face Coverage Mask Culling](3397-face-coverage-mask-culling.md) removes hidden faces of partial voxel shapes (such as stairs or slabs) by representing face coverage as a 16-bit bitmask. Unlike generic boolean solid/empty flags, this method operates at sub-face granularity (4x4 grid), allowing precise culling of geometry occluded by neighbors while preserving exposed portions of the same face.

### [ChunkMesh Vertex Packing and Management](3566-chunkmesh-vertex-packing-and-management.md)
[ChunkMesh Vertex Packing and Management](3566-chunkmesh-vertex-packing-and-management.md) is a dynamic mesh generation technique that packs vertex attributes into dense 32-bit integer formats to minimize GPU memory bandwidth. It solves the problem of sparse, high-latency vertex buffer updates by using free-list allocators, allowing incremental face addition and removal without reallocation. It sets itself apart by managing the underlying vertex data structure and GPU buffer synchronization.

### [Voxel Backface Culling and Internal Face Masking](4569-voxel-backface-culling-and-internal-face-masking.md)
[Voxel Backface Culling and Internal Face Masking](4569-voxel-backface-culling-and-internal-face-masking.md) optimizes rendering by rejecting faces that are either occluded by adjacent voxels (internal faces) or oriented away from the camera (backfaces). It distinguishes itself by performing visibility tests in projection space to determine front/back orientation, while using a compact bitmask to track internal occlusion, allowing for efficient geometry shader-based culling.

### [Block Visibility Culling](5334-block-visibility-culling.md)
[Block Visibility Culling](5334-block-visibility-culling.md) determines which voxel blocks require mesh updates based on the camera's position and rotation, avoiding unnecessary geometry generation when the camera has not moved significantly. It operates at the coarse block level by comparing current camera coordinates and orientation against previous frame values, serving as a high-level optimization that complements finer-grained [face culling](#8735-face-culling.md).

### [Extraction of Surface Points (Sobierajski)](5721-extraction-of-surface-points-sobierajski.md)
[Extraction of Surface Points (Sobierajski)](5721-extraction-of-surface-points-sobierajski.md) is a fast display method for direct rendering of boundary surfaces by extracting only visible boundary voxels from volume data. It sets itself apart by operating on a pre-extracted list of surface points rather than generating faces per voxel, and from [Voxel Block Shape & Culling Configuration](2176-voxel-block-shape-culling-configuration.md) by using orthographic visibility checks to prune the voxel list before projection.

### [Mask Projection Culling](6836-mask-projection-culling.md)
[Mask Projection Culling](6836-mask-projection-culling.md) is a visibility-based mesh filtering technique that removes vertices and faces not consistently observed across multiple camera poses by projecting 3D points into camera space and comparing their depth against rendered depth maps and binary masks. It differs from neighbor-based culling methods by relying on external camera views rather than local voxel adjacency, and from [Block Visibility Culling](5334-block-visibility-culling.md) by operating on individual mesh primitives rather than coarse chunks.

### [Mesh Culling via 3D Projection and Connected Components](6963-mesh-culling-via-3d-projection-and-connected-components.md)
[Mesh Culling via 3D Projection and Connected Components](6963-mesh-culling-via-3d-projection-and-connected-components.md) removes geometric artifacts and occluded geometry from a 3D mesh by projecting its vertices into multiple camera views and comparing their depths against reference depth maps. It classifies mesh faces as "seen," "unseen," or "forecast" and culls those that do not meet visibility criteria. It is distinct from neighbor-based culling because it relies on multi-view consistency rather than local voxel adjacency, making it suitable for unbounded reconstructions like [Gaussian Splatting](#946-gaussian-splatting.md).

### [Opacity-based Mesh Culling](8759-opacity-based-mesh-culling.md)
[Opacity-based Mesh Culling](8759-opacity-based-mesh-culling.md) reduces the complexity of polygonal mesh representations of volumetric scenes by discarding geometric primitives that contribute negligible visual information. Unlike sibling methods that rely on spatial occupancy or face coverage masks, this method evaluates the radiometric contribution (opacity) of individual triangles or faces. It sets itself apart by operating on the final extracted mesh geometry rather than the voxel grid, achieving drastic reductions in mesh count while preserving visual fidelity.

### [From-Region Visibility Preprocessing](9048-from-region-visibility-preprocessing.md)
[From-Region Visibility Preprocessing](9048-from-region-visibility-preprocessing.md) is a technique that precomputes the visibility of geometric primitives from specific regions of the viewing space to accelerate rendering. It solves the problem of expensive per-frame [visibility culling](#6226-visibility-culling.md) by shifting the computational load to an offline or semi-offline phase. Unlike sibling methods that rely on voxel adjacency or block-level occupancy, this approach operates on continuous geometry or 2.5D/3D scene representations, focusing on occluder fusion and region-based culling.

## Background
The concept of removing interior polygons to improve rendering performance originated in early voxel-based terrain generation systems, such as those used in Minecraft-like engines [S1, unofficial]. The initial implementation involved creating a class that generates cubes from triangles and checks for solid neighbors; if a neighbor exists, the side adjacent to that neighbor is not rendered [S1, unofficial]. This optimization was crucial for replacing brute-force model instantiation with reconstructed geometry, significantly reducing the number of triangles processed [S1, unofficial]. The technique evolved to support complex block shapes, transparency handling, and GPU-accelerated mesh assembly [S1, unofficial][S3, unofficial].
